order_pair.name: Order Pair
order_pair.description: One word over two operations, and only one of them cares. Three artifacts declare an axis called order in two vocabularies - VectorSubtraction and example_1_3_vector_subtraction_vr say a_minus_b | b_minus_a | reciprocal, animatedcubebuilder says ascend | descend | together - and the two vector names are two separate scenes on two separate scripts that copied one another's value list character for character, which the second one says in its own header. On the vector side the order is read by the arithmetic: head - tail is a different vector when head and tail swap, exactly the negative of the first, so the word changes the ANSWER. On the cube side the order is read by the animation and by nothing else: _finish() under the shipped closure strata hides nothing, so ascend, descend and together each end with the same 8 corner handles, the same 12 edge cylinders and the same 12 triangles standing. Three routes, one object. This bench builds both cases on one 1.16 x 0.524 x 0.60 m plate split by a seam wall: the subtraction in relief on a board at the left, the cube built from the source's own three lists at the right, and a three-slot course of plinths carrying the assembly order as real geometry. The cube's result is drawn under every value because it does not depend on one; the vector's result is drawn only under a vector value because it cannot be drawn without naming one. That asymmetry is the thesis and it produces the designed null: in the result reading, ascend, descend and together are one photograph. No RandomNumberGenerator, no randf, no noise, no _process, no Timer, no await - which matters because all three sources are clocks.
dev_themes: order as a word with two grammars
the difference between a history and an outcome
a null that is the argument rather than a check on it
interactions: walk the order axis at reading=result and watch half of it go silent: a_minus_b, b_minus_a and reciprocal each put a different arrow on the left board, and ascend, descend and together put nothing anywhere, because the only body they would add is the cube and the cube is already standing and is the same cube for all three

put reciprocal beside a_minus_b and beside b_minus_a in the result reading. It is not a third order, it is the union of the other two: the same computation as a_minus_b with the b_minus_a arrow added. The picture is literally the two singletons superimposed

switch to reading=path at ascend and at descend: the same three miniatures - eight corners, twelve edges, twelve faces - standing in opposite slots. Then together, where all three crowd into slot 0 and the other two plinths stand bare, because _phase_order() returns an empty array

compare (together, path) with the cube standing at the right under (together, result): the miniature in slot 0 is the whole cube. together's route and together's destination are the same object at two sizes, which is what having no route looks like

read the two halves against each other at any single value. The left half's arrow flips through the origin between a_minus_b and b_minus_a and the right half does not move at all between ascend and descend. That is the whole sentence
order_pair.capacity: SEE that `order` is one word carrying two grammars - in one operation it selects an outcome, in the other it selects only a history - and that a family can share a word across two vocabularies without ever having to notice that the word does different work in each, because the still that would show it was never taken

spatial_needs.footprint_note: THE STAGE IS THE FOOTPRINT AND IT IS DRAWN BEFORE EITHER AXIS IS CONSULTED: a 1.16 x 0.60 m plate 0.024 m thick, two 0.54 x 0.50 x 0.018 m boards standing on it at x = +-0.28 and z = -0.28, a 0.014 x 0.060 x 0.52 m seam wall on the centre line, and three 0.150 x 0.012 x 0.160 m course plinths at z = 0.20. The boards are the reason the AABB is a constant: they are 0.524 m tall, and the tallest thing either axis can draw is the step-2 walk marker at 0.518 m - a 0.036 m block centred on the difference tip at y = 0.500 - with the difference arrowhead itself at 0.500 m, the cube topping out at 0.443 m and the tallest course miniature at 0.174 m. The plate is the reason the plan is a constant: the widest drawn thing is the course row at x = 0.04 to 0.52 and the deepest is the plinth row at z = 0.28. Verified on a Python replica of the same constants: the union of every body in every one of the eighteen cells is exactly x -0.580..0.580, y 0.000..0.524, z -0.300..0.300 - the plate and the boards, nothing else. THE FIGURE INSIDE THE STAGE MOVES A GREAT DEAL: the left half draws one arrow at a_minus_b and four bodies at (reciprocal, both), and the right half draws one cube at result, three miniatures at (ascend, path) and one at (together, path). The world box is 1.16 x 0.524 x 0.60 in all eighteen. layout=ladder stands all six orders in a row at 1.24 m pitch, about 7.4 m wide, and is a design view rather than a map placement.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry in a Python replica built from the same constants; no Godot was run. The box is the STAGE and nothing else: the plate spans x at +-0.58 and z at +-0.30, and the tallest things in any cell are the two boards at PLATE_T + BOARD_H = 0.524. Nothing either axis draws can exceed that - every arrow is clipped inside the board by construction (max reach 0.96 x 0.235 = 0.2256 m from an origin at y = 0.274, i.e. 0.500 at the top and 0.048 at the bottom against a board running 0.024 to 0.524), the tallest single body is the 0.036 m step-2 walk marker centred on that top tip at 0.518, the cube half-diagonal in y is 0.15 + 0.019 about a centre at 0.274, and the course miniatures stand 0.174 m tall including their corner blocks on 0.012 m plinths. The replica unions every body of all eighteen cells and returns exactly the plate and the boards: x -0.580..0.580, y 0.000..0.524, z -0.300..0.300.

dna.default: order=a_minus_b, reading=result. a_minus_b because BOTH VECTOR MEMBERS SHIP IT - VectorSubtraction.gd:39 and example_1_3_vector_subtraction_vr.gd:59 both declare `= "a_minus_b"` - and because it is the literal `vector_a - vector_b` that was welded into both benches' _process before either was promoted, so it is the reading every one of the nine existing placements across the family actually renders. The cube member's default is `ascend` and it is equally shipped, but the axis has to open on one vocabulary and the vector one is two members to one. reading=result because the finished thing is what all three sources draw: none of them has ever drawn a route. VectorSubtraction's tip-to-tail chain and parallelogram closure are its OTHER axis (`construction`), and animatedcubebuilder draws its sequence only as a running animation that no still can hold. NOTE WHAT THE DEFAULT CELL COSTS: (a_minus_b, result) is the plainest tile in the sheet - the stage plus one green arrow plus the cube - and it is the cell every existing placement of the family already looks like. That is the right place to solve framing on here, because framing is set by the stage and the stage is identical in all eighteen cells.
dna.note:
WHAT THE VALUES MEAN, which member each came from, and whether the order changes the RESULT or only the PATH.

THE FAMILY FIRST, and it is a census before it is an argument. Three artifacts declare an axis called `order`, in TWO vocabularies of three words each. THE TWO VECTOR NAMES ARE NOT ONE SCENE - checked, not assumed: algorithms/vectors/04_vector_subtraction/VectorSubtraction.tscn runs VectorSubtraction.gd, which extends algorithms/vectors/shared/vector_scene_base.gd and builds three grabbable arrow rigs plus a RigidBody3D balance beam; algorithms/vectors/noc_ch01/example_1_3_vector_subtraction_vr.tscn runs a script that extends Node3D and builds three 0.1 m cylinders and a Label3D. Two scenes, two scripts, two different arrow geometries, three placements against six. What they share is the WORD and the VALUE LIST, and the younger one says so in its own header: both taken 'character for character from the sibling bench VectorSubtraction'. A DECLARED LINEAGE, not a hidden one-scene-many-names family - and the sibling test applies, because their `order` code is line for line the same decision, so they must measure alike on it.

THE THING THE CODE SAYS THAT THE BRIEF DID NOT, and it is the finding. The brief said the axis holds two cases where order has opposite consequences. True. But it also said the two interesting values are `reciprocal` and `together` because neither is simply an order - and the code says something sharper than that: NEITHER IS AN ORDER AT ALL, AND BOTH ARE THE SAME MOVE. Each vocabulary's third value is that vocabulary's UNION.

  `reciprocal` does not swap anything. In BOTH vector members the operand swap is guarded on the literal string: `var head = a; var tail = b; if order == "b_minus_a": head = b; tail = a`. Under `reciprocal` head is still a and tail is still b, so the computation is a_minus_b's, untouched. What the value adds is a SECOND ARROW at -diff, instantiated only for it (_ensure_reverse_vector / _apply_order, amber in both files). reciprocal's picture is a_minus_b's picture PLUS b_minus_a's arrow. AND THE WORD IS WRONG: the reciprocal of a vector is not defined, and the arrow drawn is the ADDITIVE inverse -(a-b). Two benches copied the wrong word character for character. Kept here because it is the family's word; corrected in `declines`.

  `together` does not reverse anything either. animatedcubebuilder's _phase_order() returns an EMPTY ARRAY for it, and start_animation() reads that empty array as: create the triangles, make every sphere, every line and every triangle visible in one frame, set COMPLETE, call _finish(). There is no sequence.

SO BOTH VOCABULARIES PUT AN ALL-RUNGS VALUE INSIDE THEIR AXIS, independently, and that habit rather than the word `order` is what the two halves of this family actually share. Both are kept here rather than fixtured out, and the reason is exact: the rule against all-rungs values is about AABB INFLATION, and neither of these inflates anything - reciprocal is one more arrow inside a board that is 0.524 m tall whatever happens on it, and together is a superposition inside one 0.150 m slot. The value that WOULD have inflated the box is `layout=ladder`, and that is an export outside both axes, pinned by the fixture.

ORDER, six values, three from each vocabulary, every one a word its own member ships.

  a_minus_b   VectorSubtraction and example_1_3_vector_subtraction_vr. head = a, tail = b - the literal `vector_a - vector_b` both benches had welded into _process. CHANGES-RESULT. The green difference arrow runs from the shared origin to (-0.24, 0.96) in figure units, i.e. up and slightly left, and it is the single body that separates this cell from a cube cell.
  b_minus_a   the same two members. head = b, tail = a. CHANGES-RESULT, and it changes it in the strongest way a still can show: the difference is the EXACT negative, so the arrow is the same length on the same line through the origin in the opposite sense. Subtraction is anti-commutative, not merely non-commutative, and the picture says which.
  reciprocal  the same two members. CHANGES-RESULT - it changes how many results are on the table, not which one is computed. Both differences at once, drawn from the shared origin, tips 2|a-b| apart on one line. The sources call this 'nose to nose through the origin', which is loose: they are TAIL to tail and their noses are as far apart as the figure allows. The picture is the exact union of the a_minus_b and b_minus_a cells.
  ascend      animatedcubebuilder. _phase_order() -> ["vertices", "edges", "triangles"], the shipped chain, at the shipped timings (vertices 0.5 s each, edges 0.2 s, triangles 0.15 s). CHANGES-PATH-ONLY. Its course reads left to right: eight corners, then twelve edges, then twelve faces - 0D, 1D, 2D, the member's own truth line, 'dimension accumulates'.
  descend     animatedcubebuilder. -> ["triangles", "edges", "vertices"], the same machine backwards, arguing the opposite ('a solid DECOMPOSES'). CHANGES-PATH-ONLY. Its course is the same three miniatures in the opposite slots. It is not the vertical mirror of ascend, because the phases are 8, 12 and 12 pieces rather than three equal bands.
  together    animatedcubebuilder. -> [], no phases at all. CHANGES-PATH-ONLY, and it deletes the path rather than reversing it. All three miniatures crowd into slot 0, which superimposed is the whole cube, and slots 1 and 2 stand bare. together's route IS its destination, at 0.433 of the size.

AND THAT IS THE SENTENCE: three values of one axis change what the answer is, and three change only how it was reached. The word does not distinguish them and neither vocabulary has any way to notice, because a-b and b-a live in two files that were never photographed beside a cube.

READING, three values, and `result` is the one that carries the thesis because it is where a path-only order has nothing left to say.

  result  the finished thing. The cube, ALWAYS - under every value of `order`, because its result does not depend on one - and the difference arrow, ONLY under a vector value, because there is no such thing as 'the difference of a and b' until an order picks which is the head. That asymmetry is not a layout choice, it is the argument made structural, and it is what makes the null a null. This is where CHANGES-PATH-ONLY collapses to nothing.
  path    the route, and only the route. For a vector word, the walk: out along the head, then back along the tail, with a size-graded block at each of the three waypoints. For a cube word, the three assembly courses. The finished cube is NOT drawn here - a route is not its destination - so this is the one reading where the right half can be a row of miniatures on plinths with nothing above them.
  both    the result standing in front of the route it was reached by. The walk is built at 0.016 m of extra relief so that its first leg, which is the same segment as one of the two operands, stands proud of it instead of z-fighting with it. The busiest cell in the sheet is (reciprocal, both): two operands, two differences, two walks and six markers.

HOW THE SHEET IS PROTECTED FROM THE COLOUR TRAP, and it cost a change to the sources' own palette. The critic measures luminance by default and only rescues a colour-only pair afterwards. BOTH VECTOR MEMBERS DRAW THE COUNTER-DIFFERENCE IN Color(1.0, 0.85, 0.35) AGAINST A DIFFERENCE OF Color(0.55, 1.0, 0.4) - Rec.709 0.846 against 0.861, ISOLUMINANT TO WITHIN 0.015. In greyscale their `reciprocal` is two identical arrows and the second one cannot be told from the first. The counter arrow here is darkened to 0.638 so the union reads as a union of two different arrows and so the two reciprocal pairs are ORDERED rather than tied. The full ladder: board 0.139, plate 0.180, plinth 0.250, face1 0.276, face2 0.321, b 0.331, face0 0.358, a 0.398, seam 0.430, walk-counter 0.440, origin 0.510, walk 0.617, counter 0.638, corner 0.651, difference 0.861, edge 0.939. No two bodies that TOUCH sit within 0.10 of each other; the closest pair is a 0.398 against b 0.331 at the shared origin, and those two are drawn in all eighteen cells, so no measured pair ever depends on telling them apart.

THE THESIS SOMEONE COULD DISAGREE WITH: `order` is not one axis wearing one word, it is two axes wearing one word - one that selects an outcome and one that selects only a history - and a family that shares the word across both has published a distinction it cannot see. THE DISAGREEMENT AVAILABLE, and it is fair: a reader can say that order-of-assembly is a real and teachable property of the cube, that animatedcubebuilder is an ANIMATION artifact whose whole subject is a process, and that judging it by what a still holds is judging it by the wrong instrument. The answer is that the member's own @identity names 'the animation sequence' as its critical parameter and its own truth line is 'dimension accumulates' - a claim about an ORDER, made by an artifact whose finished object records none of it - and that the three placements of it in the corpus are all shipped at closure=strata, where _finish() does nothing. The cell where holding the thesis costs something is (together, path), which photographs as a small complete cube: the honest drawing of 'no sequence' is indistinguishable from the honest drawing of 'finished', and that is a point against the axis rather than for it.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: ascend against descend, in the result reading
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic:
THE CONTEXT IS THE `result` COLUMN AND THE RANKING IS COMPUTED INSIDE IT. Six values give fifteen pairs there; three of them are exactly zero and this is one.

WHY IT IS ZERO AND NOT MERELY SMALL. Under reading=result the builder draws the stage, then the cube, then - only if the active word is one of a_minus_b, b_minus_a, reciprocal - a difference arrow. `ascend`, `descend` and `together` are all cube words, so all three draw the stage and the cube and stop. _build_result() branches on VECTOR_WORDS.has(word) and nothing else; _build_cube() takes a centre, a side and a scale and never reads `order` at any depth. There is no generator anywhere in the file - no RandomNumberGenerator, no randf, no FastNoiseLite - so two builds of one cell are the same mesh, and three builds of three cube words are the same mesh three times. Predicted 0.00 percent focus and 0.00 percent frame.

THE CEILING IS 0.05 PERCENT, and it is tight on purpose. Anything above it is not a finding, it is a BUG, and there are only three places it could be: (a) a stray read of `order` inside the cube path, (b) a build that is not deterministic, which for this file would have to mean a Godot-side ordering effect rather than a draw, or (c) the sweep failing to set the value at all, in which case every cell is the default and the whole sheet is one frame rather than four. Check _rejects.json first - all three exports are String enums and Object.set() on a typed property of the wrong type is refused in SILENCE - but note that this artifact's values are all words with no numeric reading, so cabinet_sweep.coerce() cannot numericise any of them, which is the one way that failure has ever bitten.

THE OTHER TWO ZEROS ARE THE SAME FACT: ascend against together and descend against together, both 0.00, for the same reason. Three cells, one photograph.

THE CONTRAST THAT MUST HOLD ALONGSIDE, AND IT IS THE REAL NUMBER TO ARGUE WITH. In the same `result` column the closest NON-ZERO pair is A_MINUS_B AGAINST RECIPROCAL, PREDICTED 6.5 PERCENT. The two frames are identical except for one added arrow, the counter-difference at -(a-b), because reciprocal runs the a_minus_b computation untouched and only adds a body.

THE ARITHMETIC, on a Python replica of the same constants. Camera is capture_config_sweep's: FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, framing 0.58 on the union AABB, which is the STAGE at 1.16 x 0.524 x 0.60. Screen basis at that standpoint: x-hat -> (0.8139, 0.1494), z-hat -> (0.5810, 0.2092), y-hat -> (0, 0.9664). The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes - identical here, because the stage is - so the framing value does not enter the number at all; only the subject box does. That box is the plate corners and the two board tops projected: 1.29272 x 0.68125 = 0.88066 m2.

The added arrow: |a - b| = 0.23254 m, drawn from 0.018 m clear of the origin to a 0.050 m head, so a 0.16454 m rod plus a head. The direction -(a-b) projects to screen with a length ratio of 0.9227, giving a 0.15182 m rod on screen. The rod is a box 0.026 m in-plane by 0.026 m of relief; the in-plane normal projects 0.8525 onto the screen perpendicular and z-hat projects 0.6123, so the silhouette is 0.026 x 0.8525 + 0.026 x 0.6123 = 0.03808 m wide. Rod 0.15182 x 0.03808 = 0.005782 m2; head, a triangular prism 0.046 m across and 0.050 m long, 0.001639 m2. Total 0.007421 m2 = 0.8427 percent of the subject box.

The critic greys, neutralises each frame's own corner, resizes to 160 x 160 = 25600 px and takes the mean of the hottest 5 percent = 1280 px. 0.8427 percent of 25600 is 215.7 changed pixels, FAR LESS than the 1280-pixel window, so THE NUMBER IS SET BY AREA, NOT BY CONTRAST - the opposite of the usual case, and it means a brighter arrow would not help much while a thicker one would. The arrow stands on the board over its whole length (it runs from y 0.274 down to 0.048 against a board spanning 0.024 to 0.524), so the contrast is counter 0.638 against board 0.139 = 0.499 of albedo separation; applying the lighting-and-tonemap compression the substance_room replica measured at 0.77 gives 0.3842. 215.7 x 38.42 / 1280 = 6.47. Registered at 6.5.

WHY THAT PAIR AND NOT ANOTHER, ranked on the replica inside the same column: a_minus_b/reciprocal 6.5, cube-word/a_minus_b and cube-word/b_minus_a 9.4 (one whole difference arrow at the brighter 0.861), cube-word/reciprocal 11.0, b_minus_a/reciprocal 12.3 (an arrow added AND the -D arrow recoloured from 0.861 to 0.638), a_minus_b/b_minus_a 18.7 (the arrow leaves one place and appears in another). The named pair is the floor of the live part of the column by 2.9 points.

THE PREDICTION IS A FLOOR, NOT A FORECAST. The replica has one key, flat shading, no shadows, no AO, no antialiasing, and every prior prediction in this corpus under-read by 1.5x to 6.7x. IF THE SWEEP COMES BACK BELOW 6.5 ON a_minus_b/reciprocal, STOP AND INVESTIGATE THE HARNESS BEFORE THE DESIGN: (a) tools/check_dna_declarations.py, because a value the code cannot reach falls back to the default and prints identical tiles; (b) _rejects.json; (c) whether the sheet was captured with --max=18, because at build_dna_gallery's default cap of 9 the 6 x 3 cross product is trimmed from the tail of the LATER axis and `reading` collapses to [result] alone - which happens to keep this prediction and the null, and deletes every body that explains either of them.

designed_nulls.why: IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION AND IT IS THE THESIS, not a spare check. animatedcubebuilder's _finish() under the shipped closure `strata` does nothing at all - its own comment says 'nothing is hidden, all three layers are left standing' - so the ascend chain and the descend chain end with the same 8 vertex handles, the same 12 edge cylinders and the same 12 triangles visible. The order lives in the ANIMATION and the animation is over. In this bench the result reading therefore draws the stage and the cube and stops, for both words, from the same _build_cube() call with the same three arguments. Predicted 0.00 percent focus and 0.00 percent frame. Anything above 0.05 percent means a read of `order` has leaked into the cube path or the build is not deterministic; anything above 2 percent means the sweep never set the value and nothing else in the sheet can be believed until it is found. THE CONTRAST THAT MUST HOLD ALONGSIDE IT: the same two words under reading=path must be among the widest pairs in the sheet, because there the three miniatures stand in opposite slots. A null that held under `path` as well would mean the course builder is not reading the phase list either.

The same fact from the other side, and the sharper one. `together` is not a reversed order, it is NO order: _phase_order() returns an empty array and start_animation() reveals everything in one frame. So the two words differ in whether there was a sequence at all, and the finished object still cannot tell you - because the finished object is what BOTH of them finish with. Predicted 0.00 percent. If the three cube words are ever anything but one photograph in the result reading, this artifact has a bug rather than a finding.
The third pair of the same three-way, registered so the closure is complete rather than assumed from the other two. Three cells, one photograph, zero to the byte.

dna.designed_nulls_why:
THREE NULLS, ONE FACT, AND IT IS THE ARGUMENT RATHER THAN A CHECK ON IT. Cube-building commutes in its result, so in the reading that shows only results its entire vocabulary is one tile. That is the sentence the bench exists to say, and it is worth noticing that the sentence is only sayable because the OTHER half of the family, sharing the same word, does not collapse: in the same column a_minus_b, b_minus_a and reciprocal are three distinct tiles separated by 6.5 to 18.7 percent. Same axis, same reading, one vocabulary alive and one dead.

NO PAIR ON THE VECTOR SIDE COLLAPSES, IN EITHER READING, AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN HOPED. In `result` the three frames are {+D}, {-D} and {+D, -D counter}: the singletons differ by two arrow-areas, and each differs from the union by one. In `path` they are walk(a,b), walk(b,a) and both walks: the two walks leave the origin in different directions (50 degrees against -14 degrees), turn at different waypoints and land at opposite tips, so no two of the three share a body except the origin marker. The brief asked whether any vector pair collapses. None does, and the reason is exactly why the axis belongs on that member: the operation reads the order.

THE TEMPTING FOURTH NULL WAS REFUSED AND IS RECORDED AS A DECLINE. Making the counter-difference the same colour as the difference would have made `reciprocal` the EXACT pixel-union of the two singletons, which is a prettier statement of the union - and it would have tied the two reciprocal pairs to the byte, because |D| = |-D| and the two arrows project to identical screen areas from this standpoint. A tie is not a closest pair; it is a coin flip that the critic reports as a fact. The colours were separated instead.
dna.fixture_why: The bench can stand all six orders in a row (layout=ladder, 1.24 m pitch, about 7.4 m wide) but the SWEEP must see one at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so a six-wide row in the same spec would frame every single cell against seven and a half metres and photograph the 0.026 m arrows as hairs and the 0.020 m edge rods as nothing. layout is an export and not an axis, and it ships at single, so the fixture is a belt over braces. IT IS ALSO THE ONLY ALL-RUNGS THING HERE, WHICH IS WORTH SAYING PLAINLY, BECAUSE BOTH VOCABULARIES PUT AN ALL-RUNGS VALUE INSIDE THEIR AXIS: `reciprocal` draws both differences and `together` reveals every phase at once. Neither is fixtured out and neither should be, because the rule they appear to break is about AABB inflation and neither inflates - one is a second arrow inside a board that is 0.524 m tall whatever stands on it, the other is a superposition inside a 0.150 m slot. WHAT IS NOT FIXTURED, AND WHY NOTHING NEEDS TO BE: there is no clock and no draw. No RandomNumberGenerator, no randf, no FastNoiseLite, deliberately no NoiseTexture2D, no _process, no Timer, no tween and no await. That matters because ALL THREE SOURCES ARE CLOCKS and two of them are unphotographable without one: VectorSubtraction recomputes every frame in _process from live grab-sphere positions, example_1_3 recomputes every frame from two exported Vector3s, and animatedcubebuilder is a state machine with an 0.5 s initial delay, a 3.0 s await inside setup_scene() and per-item steps of 0.5 / 0.2 / 0.15 s - so what a still of THAT member shows is a fact about the shutter. Its `order` axis was promoted anyway, in 2026-07-29, and this bench is the first thing in the corpus that can photograph what the axis is worth.
dna.kin: The three sources are the kin, and the relation is two relations rather than one. The two vector benches are SIBLINGS: same operation, same word, same three values, two scenes, and the younger one declares the borrowing in its own header - so the honest expectation is that they measure ALIKE on `order`, which is itself a check on the shared vocabulary. animatedcubebuilder is not a sibling of either; it is a member only of the word. Its @identity truth line is 'dimension accumulates - points make edges, edges make faces, faces make solids', which is a claim about an ORDER; VectorSubtraction's is 'subtraction is directional memory - a-b is the vector that, if you followed b, would tell you where a is', which is a claim about a DIRECTION that an order determines. Read side by side those two sentences are the axis: one says the sequence is the meaning, the other says the sequence chooses the answer, and only the second leaves a mark on the finished thing. A room holding this bench beside VectorSubtraction is saying the same sentence twice about vectors; a room holding it beside animatedcubebuilder is the comparison neither of them can perform, because one is a 1.5 m arrow rig on grab spheres and the other is a 1 m cube on a 4-second timer in a different scene. ON THE VALUE SIDE this is a two-vocabulary family with no shared word below the axis name, which makes it the opposite case to the corpus's unanimous-vocabulary families: there, five words agreed across three members and the disagreement was in the geometry; here the geometries are honest and it is the WORD that is doing two jobs.
declines: THE BRIEF'S QUESTION ABOUT `reciprocal`, answered against the guess. It asked whether reciprocal is 1/a, the reversed pair, or something else. IT IS NEITHER OF THE FIRST TWO. It does not reverse the pair - the operand swap in both members is guarded on the literal string "b_minus_a", so under reciprocal head is still a and tail is still b and the computed difference is a - b, unchanged. What it does is ADD a second arrow at -diff, built only for that value. It is the UNION of the other two values, not a third alternative, and it is therefore an all-rungs value sitting inside the axis - which CLAUDE.md's own lesson says never to do. And the word is simply wrong: the reciprocal of a vector is undefined; -(a-b) is the ADDITIVE inverse. Two benches shipped the wrong word, one having copied it from the other character for character. It is kept because renaming it here would break the only thing the two vocabularies have, which is that each member's own words are on the axis.

THE BRIEF'S QUESTION ABOUT `together`, answered the same way. It asked whether together is an all-rungs or simultaneous value. IT IS SIMULTANEOUS AND IT IS ALL-RUNGS, and _phase_order() says so in one line by returning []. start_animation() then reveals every sphere, every line and every triangle in a single frame and goes straight to COMPLETE. It is not fixtured out, because the reason to fixture an all-rungs value is that it inflates the AABB and makes the camera move between cells, and this one does not: superimposed in slot 0 the three phases are exactly the cube, 0.13 m on a side, inside a stage that is 1.16 m wide before anything is drawn.

A TIME-DOMAIN DRAWING OF THE CUBE ORDER, which is what the source actually has and which a still cannot hold. animatedcubebuilder's whole argument is 0.5 s per vertex, 0.2 s per edge, 0.15 s per triangle, behind a 0.5 s initial delay and a 3.0 s await. Photographing THAT means photographing a clock, and the same still taken 200 ms later is a different picture with no axis in it. The course is the repair: the order is drawn as PLACE instead of as time - three plinths are three slots, and a phase stands in the slot it was revealed in. It is a translation and it is declared as one. The cost is that `together`, having one slot, photographs as a small complete cube, so the drawing of 'no sequence' and the drawing of 'finished' look alike - which is a true thing about the value and is written down rather than designed around.

THE SOURCES' AMBER. Both vector members draw the counter-difference in Color(1.0, 0.85, 0.35) against a difference of Color(0.55, 1.0, 0.4): Rec.709 0.846 against 0.861, isoluminant to within 0.015. In greyscale their entire `reciprocal` value is two arrows that cannot be told apart, which is the colour trap this corpus has been bitten by before. Darkened here to 0.638. That change also breaks a tie that would otherwise have been exact: |a-b| = |b-a| and the two arrows project to identical screen areas from the canonical standpoint, so with one colour the two reciprocal pairs would have measured the same to the byte and the reported closest pair would have been a coin flip.

THE SOURCE'S THIRD FACE COLOUR. animatedcubebuilder rotates its twelve triangles through Color(0.8,0.2,0.4), Color(0.8,0.1,0.1) and Color(0.1,0.1,0.1) at alpha 0.6. The third is 0.100 luminance, which opaque against a 0.139 board photographs as a hole rather than as a face - four of the twelve triangles would go missing from the picture. Raised to 0.321. The rotation, the order of the twelve triangles and the modulo-3 rule are the source's own and are kept exactly.

TRANSPARENT FACES. The source draws its triangles at alpha 0.6 with CULL_DISABLED so a learner in the headset can see the scaffold through them. Opaque shrunken patches are used instead - each triangle scaled 0.60 toward its own centroid - because a transparency sort is a rendering-order fact and two builds of one cell must be the same picture, and because the shrink keeps the corners and the edges visible around every face, which is what the shipped `strata` ending is FOR. The diagonal seam between each face's two triangles stays open, so the picture still reports 12 rather than 6.

ANIMATEDCUBEBUILDER'S SECOND AXIS, `closure` (strata | scaffold | solid), which is a real axis and is deliberately not on this bench. It is a fact about what the build LEAVES, not about the order it ran in, and putting it here would let a reader explain the null away: with closure=solid the finished cube is one shaded mesh whatever the order, and with closure=scaffold the faces are hidden whatever the order, so all three closures collapse the cube vocabulary equally. Including it would have added a second reason for the null and made the first one unprovable. The bench builds `strata` only, which is the shipped default and the value all three existing placements use.

THE VECTOR MEMBERS' OTHER AXIS, `construction` (flip | chain | parallelogram | bare), for the same reason and one more. It is the artifact's answer to 'what is subtraction ARGUED to be', not to 'which subtraction', and one of its four readings - `chain`, the walk out along the head and back along the tail - is exactly the path this bench needed, so it appears here as the PATH reading rather than as a rival axis. That is a borrowing and it is declared: the walk drawn here is the members' `chain`, with markers added.

THE MEMBERS' SCALE AND THEIR OPERANDS. VectorSubtraction spawns a = (1.6, 0.7, -0.4) and b = (-0.3, 1.1, 0.8) in a 1.5 m axis frame at scale 0.5; example_1_3 exports a = (0.2, 0.15, 0) and b = (-0.1, 0.25, 0) in a 0.75 m frame; animatedcubebuilder builds a 1.0 m cube. None of those numbers is shared here. The figure is rebuilt at 0.235 m per unit from a = (0.62, 0.74) and b = (0.86, -0.22), chosen so the difference is NEARLY VERTICAL - a - b = (-0.24, 0.96) - because the anti-commutative pair then reads as one line through the origin taken in two senses, which is the most legible thing a still can say about the sign of an order. The members' vectors are three-dimensional and generic; theirs would have projected to two arrows at an awkward angle and buried the finding in a foreshortening.

A THIRD READING VALUE FOR THE CUBE'S OWN EXPLODED DIAGRAM, i.e. lifting the 32 pieces apart along y in assembly order. It was built on paper and refused: the corner set, the edge set and the face set each span the full 0.30 m of the cube, so separating three strata by anything less than 0.30 m interpenetrates and anything more breaks the 0.524 m stage that keeps the AABB constant. The course of miniatures says the same thing in a tenth of the height and keeps the phases whole.

GRAB SPHERES AND THE BALANCE BEAM. animatedcubebuilder's eight vertices are grab_sphere_point instances that stay live after the build so the cube can be deformed by its corners, and VectorSubtraction hangs a RigidBody3D balance beam off the origin. Both are drawn here as plain geometry - the corners as 0.038 m blocks - because a physics body emits a non-finite transform under a scaled parent (that member's own comment) and because an interactive handle photographed at rest is a block with extra risk.
dna.sweep_note: THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=18 AND THE COST OF GETTING IT WRONG IS EVERY BODY THAT EXPLAINS THE RESULT. `order` is declared first and is never trimmed; `reading` is second, and build_dna_gallery trims the LATER axis from the tail until the cross product fits its cap. At the default --max=9 the 6 x 3 sheet renders as 6 x 1 = `result` only. That happens to keep BOTH pre-registered numbers - the three-way null and the 6.5 percent closest pair - and to delete every single thing that says why either of them is true: no walk, no courses, no miniatures, three cells that are one photograph with nothing anywhere in the sheet to show what the three words differ in. It is the most dangerous trim in the corpus so far, because it leaves a finished-looking sheet whose headline measurements are correct and whose argument is missing. At --max=12 it renders 6 x 2 = result and path, which is the experiment; 18 adds `both` and the layered cells.
